indicators.title: Median home price ÷ median family income
indicators.note: Median sales price of new houses sold (Census/HUD) over median family income (Census CPS). New-house prices run above existing-house prices, so the level is high; the change over time is the point.

indicators.title: A 20% down payment on the median new home, in months of median family income
indicators.note: 20% of the median new-house price over one month of median family income, before taxes and with nothing spent. The saving hurdle before the first payment; low rates do not shrink it.

indicators.title: Mortgage payment on the median home, % of median family income
indicators.note: Principal and interest on a 30-year fixed loan at that year's average rate (Freddie Mac PMMS), 20% down, for the median new house. Excludes taxes and insurance. Captures both prices and rates: Boomers bought at high rates in the early 1980s, and this measure shows it.

indicators.title: 30-year fixed mortgage rate
indicators.note: Freddie Mac Primary Mortgage Market Survey, annual average.

indicators.title: Real hourly compensation, all workers (1948 = 100)
indicators.note: BLS, nonfarm business sector. Includes benefits and all earners from clerks to CEOs, and uses BLS's own price deflator. This is the measure on which the pay gap looks smallest.

indicators.title: Real hourly wage, production and nonsupervisory workers (1948 = 100 scale)
indicators.note: BLS average hourly earnings of the ~80% of private workers who are not supervisors, deflated by CPI-U, joined to the scale above at 1964 (the series starts then). Wages only, no benefits. This is the measure on which the pay gap looks largest.

indicators.title: Employee compensation, % of gross domestic income
indicators.note: BEA. Wages, salaries and benefits paid to employees, as a share of all income earned in the US.

indicators.title: Corporate profits after tax, % of GDP
indicators.note: BEA. Profits after tax, without inventory valuation and capital consumption adjustments.

indicators.title: Federal minimum wage in 2025 dollars
indicators.note: US Department of Labor, deflated by CPI-U. Many states and cities set higher minimums; this is the national floor.

indicators.title: Hours at the federal minimum wage to pay a year of public 4-year tuition and fees
indicators.note: In-state tuition and required fees, public 4-year institutions (NCES Digest table 330.10), sticker price before grants. Net price after aid is lower and has risen less; see the college page.

indicators.title: Public 4-year tuition and fees, 2025 dollars
indicators.note: NCES Digest table 330.10, deflated by CPI-U.

indicators.title: Federal corporate income tax, % of corporate profits
indicators.note: BEA. Federal taxes on corporate income over corporate profits before tax (book profits, not taxable income). An aggregate effective rate across all corporations, profitable or not.

indicators.title: Top federal income tax bracket rate
indicators.note: IRS Statistics of Income, historical table 23. Statutory rate on the highest bracket; few people paid it, and effective rates at the top were always lower. See the published estimates below.

sources.note: table data through 2018; 2019+ statutory 37% (P.L. 115-97, made permanent by P.L. 119-21)
